13 /-!
14 # Finite sets
15 
16 Terms of type `Finset α` are one way of talking about finite subsets of `α` in Mathlib.
17 Below, `Finset α` is defined as a structure with 2 fields:
18 
19   1. `val` is a `Multiset α` of elements;
20   2. `nodup` is a proof that `val` has no duplicates.
21 
22 Finsets in Lean are constructive in that they have an underlying `List` that enumerates their
23 elements. In particular, any function that uses the data of the underlying list cannot depend on its
24 ordering. This is handled on the `Multiset` level by multiset API, so in most cases one needn't
25 worry about it explicitly.
26 
27 Finsets give a basic foundation for defining finite sums and products over types:
28 
29   1. `∑ i ∈ (s : Finset α), f i`;
30   2. `∏ i ∈ (s : Finset α), f i`.
31 
32 Lean refers to these operations as big operators.
33 More information can be found in `Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Group/Finset/Basic.lean`.
34 
35 Finsets are directly used to define fintypes in Lean.
36 A `Fintype α` instance for a type `α` consists of a universal `Finset α` containing every term of
37 `α`, called `univ`. See `Mathlib/Data/Fintype/Basic.lean`.
38 
39 `Finset.card`, the size of a finset is defined in `Mathlib/Data/Finset/Card.lean`.
40 This is then used to define `Fintype.card`, the size of a type.
41 
42 ## File structure
43 
44 This file defines the `Finset` type and the membership and subset relations between finsets.
45 Most constructions involving `Finset`s have been split off to their own files.
46 
47 ## Main definitions
48 
49 * `Finset`: Defines a type for the finite subsets of `α`.
50   Constructing a `Finset` requires two pieces of data: `val`, a `Multiset α` of elements,
51   and `nodup`, a proof that `val` has no duplicates.
52 * `a ∈ (s : Finset α)` is defined through coercion to `Set α`.
53 
54 ## Tags
55 
56 finite sets, finset
57

72 /-- `Finset α` is the type of finite sets of elements of `α`. It is implemented
73   as a multiset (a list up to permutation) which has no duplicate elements. -/
74 structure Finset (α : Type*) where
75   /-- The underlying multiset -/
76   val : Multiset α
77   /-- `val` contains no duplicates -/
78   nodup : Nodup val
79 
80 instance Multiset.canLiftFinset {α} : CanLift (Multiset α) (Finset α) Finset.val Multiset.Nodup :=
81   ⟨fun m hm => ⟨⟨m, hm⟩, rfl⟩⟩
82 
83 namespace Finset
84 
85 theorem eq_of_veq : ∀ {s t : Finset α}, s.1 = t.1 → s = t
86   | ⟨s, _⟩, ⟨t, _⟩, h => by cases h; rfl
87 
88 theorem val_injective : Injective (val : Finset α → Multiset α) := fun _ _ => eq_of_veq
89 
90 @[simp]
91 theorem val_inj {s t : Finset α} : s.1 = t.1 ↔ s = t :=
92   val_injective.eq_iff
93 
94 instance decidableEq [DecidableEq α] : DecidableEq (Finset α)
95   | _, _ => decidable_of_iff _ val_inj
96

99 /-- Convert a finset to a set in the natural way. -/
100 instance : SetLike (Finset α) α where
101   coe s := {a | a ∈ s.1}
102   coe_injective' s₁ s₂ h := (val_inj.symm.trans <| s₁.nodup.ext s₂.nodup).2 <| Set.ext_iff.mp h
103 
104 theorem mem_def {a : α} {s : Finset α} : a ∈ s ↔ a ∈ s.1 :=
105   Iff.rfl
106 
107 -- If https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/issues/2678 is resolved-

109 @[simp, grind =]
110 theorem mem_val {a : α} {s : Finset α} : (a ∈ s.1) = (a ∈ s) := rfl
111 
112 @[simp, grind =]
113 theorem mem_mk {a : α} {s nd} : a ∈ @Finset.mk α s nd ↔ a ∈ s :=
114   Iff.rfl
115 
116 instance decidableMem [_h : DecidableEq α] (a : α) (s : Finset α) : Decidable (a ∈ s) :=
117   Multiset.decidableMem _ _
118

384 namespace List

386 variable [DecidableEq α] {a : α} {f : α → β} {s : Finset α} {t : Set β} {t' : Finset β}

388 instance [DecidablePred (· ∈ t)] : Decidable (Set.MapsTo f s t) :=
389   inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ x ∈ s, f x ∈ t))
390 
391 instance [DecidableEq β] : Decidable (Set.SurjOn f s t') :=
392   inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ x ∈ t', ∃ y ∈ s, f y = x))
